requirement:
A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:

:::{sites} skills
```yaml
language: markdown
paths: [assets/skills]
rule:
  kind: minus_metadata
match:
  - "---\nname: example\n---\n\n# Example\n"
no_match:
  - "# Example\n"
```
:::
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references` has one MAY and one MUST. The MAY lets a skill put specialized material in linked files, so there is nothing to check. The MUST is that each such link says when to read the file. Each site upholds the MUST on its own, because each bundled skill is a site with its own review. Nothing in the text needs separate code to carry it out, so no obligation falls outside both categories. The requirement has no violation queries.

**Site query `skills`.** I ran `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references/skills`. It selected exactly these five bundled skills:
- `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`

A regex search for `^name: habeas` found the same five files and no other front-matter skills. The reference files under `references/` have no front matter, so they are correctly left out. The query is limited to `assets/skills` and uses the `minus_metadata` kind, which matches the description "recognized by its front matter". I found no skills that it misses and no places outside the scope that it selects.

**Query snippets.** The match snippet is a document with front matter (`---\nname: example\n---\n\n# Example\n`). The no_match snippet is the same body without front matter (`# Example\n`). Together they show what the query selects and what nearby text it must not select.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_say_when_to_read_each_reference_file]` carries the {test} reference. It checks each link sentence in the five skills and in the reference files. A regex finds every `references/*.md` pointer in each skill file and asserts that it lies inside a checked sentence that says when to read it. It also asserts that every non-SKILL file in each skill is linked and has a check. This is more than the site-level obligation needs, and it supports the requirement rather than leaving a gap.
